executiveSummary: The audit shows a site with several families of findings that affect trust, readability, mobile use, and search visibility. Accessibility findings are the most extensive, with contrast, touch target, form labelling, and heading structure all needing attention, so visitors may struggle to read content, complete actions, or move through the site confidently. Performance findings also matter, because the main content loads slowly and the page layout moves while content appears, which can interrupt browsing and weaken the experience on key pages. Privacy and security findings add a further trust burden, because tracking begins before consent and the site lacks basic browser protections. Taken together, the findings indicate that your site would benefit most from coordinated work that improves clarity, stability, and visitor confidence across the main customer journey.

themes.title: Improve text contrast so content stays readable
themes.businessImpact: A visitor who struggles to read low-contrast text may miss key information on your pages, including opening details, room descriptions, or calls to action. That makes it harder for them to compare offers and continue toward a booking or enquiry. On mobile screens and in strong light, the same finding can affect visitors who would otherwise be able to read the page. When this appears across many pages, the reading burden becomes part of the overall experience of the site.
themes.legalRelevance: Criterion 1.4.3 (Contrast (Minimum)), WCAG 2.2 level AA, referenced by the EN 301 549 standard.
recommendedActions: The technical team managing your site should raise the foreground and background contrast for the text elements identified in the affected pages, while keeping the existing visual design consistent where possible.
Have the colour palette checked against WCAG 2.2 contrast thresholds for both normal text and larger text, so that text remains readable across the affected pages.
Review text placed over images, gradients, and coloured blocks first, because these combinations often leave visitors with the least legible content.
Where brand colours are too light to meet the required contrast, adjust the shade or use a darker text treatment, which will make the content easier to read for visitors in strong light.

themes.title: Make touch targets easier to use on mobile
themes.businessImpact: A visitor using a phone may have difficulty tapping small or tightly packed controls, which can slow navigation and lead to missed selections. That is particularly important on pages that support restaurant enquiries, room navigation, or booking decisions. When taps fail or require repeated attempts, visitors may abandon the action rather than continue. The finding therefore affects both ease of use and the likelihood that a visitor completes the next step.
themes.legalRelevance: Criterion 2.5.8 (Target Size (Minimum)), WCAG 2.2 level AA, referenced by the EN 301 549 standard.
recommendedActions: The technical team managing your site should enlarge the touch targets identified in the affected pages, or add enough spacing between them to avoid accidental taps.
Check navigation links, buttons, and icon-only controls first, because these are the elements visitors use most often on mobile devices.
If the design cannot accommodate larger controls, rework the surrounding layout so that each control remains easy to activate without overlap.
Confirm that the same spacing pattern is applied consistently across the affected pages, which will reduce the chance of missed taps during browsing.

themes.title: Help search engines understand key pages
themes.businessImpact: Search engines rely on structured signals to interpret a page and decide how to present it in results. Without those signals, the pages may be harder to classify and may be less likely to stand out when visitors search for your business, rooms, or services. A missing sitemap also makes discovery less reliable on sites where some pages are not strongly linked. For a business that depends on being found online, that can reduce visibility and weaken the path to contact or booking.
recommendedActions: The technical team managing your site should add structured data in JSON-LD format for the business, the website, and the main page types, so that search engines can understand the site more clearly.
Provide a sitemap.xml file and make sure it is referenced correctly, which will help search engines discover the affected pages more reliably.
Add a canonical URL to each indexable page, because this helps search engines choose the preferred address when similar content can be reached in more than one way.
Include the correct business entity type in the structured data, such as Hotel or Restaurant where appropriate, so that machine systems can identify the business from the page itself.

themes.title: Give forms and links clear accessible names
themes.businessImpact: A visitor who reaches a form without labels may not understand what to enter, and that can stop them from completing a request. Links without clear text are also harder to identify, which makes navigation less reliable for all visitors and especially for those using assistive technology. A page without a top-level heading is harder to scan and may leave the visitor uncertain about its main purpose. Together, these findings make simple navigation and enquiry steps less dependable.
themes.legalRelevance: Criteria 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships), 2.4.4 (Link Purpose (In Context)) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value), WCAG 2.2 level AA, referenced by the EN 301 549 standard.
recommendedActions: The technical team managing your site should add clear labels to every form control on the affected pages, so that visitors can understand what each field expects.
Have the link with non-discernible text replaced with a meaningful label, because visitors need to know where each link will take them before they activate it.
Add a single level-1 heading to each affected page, which will give the page a clear main topic for visitors and search engines.
Check that labels, headings, and link text use plain language that matches the action or destination shown on the page.

themes.title: Stabilise page layout while content loads
themes.businessImpact: When visible elements shift during loading, a visitor may click the wrong control or lose their place while reading. That creates friction during browsing and can interrupt a reservation or enquiry flow before it is complete. Real visitor data also shows that this behaviour is not limited to a lab measurement, which makes the finding more relevant to the experience your customers actually receive. If layout movement is frequent, it can reduce confidence in the page and make the site feel harder to use.
recommendedActions: The technical team managing your site should reserve space for images, banners, and other late-loading elements on the affected pages, so that the layout stays steady as content appears.
Inspect the main content area first, because the largest visible shifts usually have the strongest effect on reading and clicking.
Review any elements inserted after the page begins loading, and load them in a way that does not push existing content out of place.
Where dynamic blocks must appear late, keep their dimensions consistent across states, which will reduce movement for visitors.

themes.title: Speed up the main content that visitors wait for
themes.businessImpact: Visitors judge a page quickly, and slow loading of the main content can make them wait before they can read or act. That delay affects room pages, service pages, and the home page alike, so it can interrupt the path from interest to enquiry. The site also shows slower interaction and slower visual progress on some pages, which suggests a broader loading burden rather than a single isolated case. For a visitor comparing options, that extra wait can be enough to move on to another site.
recommendedActions: The technical team managing your site should first reduce the time before the main content appears, because that is the key loading delay identified for these pages.
Prioritise the resources needed for the visible top section, so that the first meaningful content appears sooner for visitors.
Review large images, web fonts, and other blocking assets after that first step, because they can still slow the display once the main loading path is improved.
Trim unused code and delay non-essential scripts where possible, which will help the page become usable sooner for visitors.

themes.title: Stop tracking and cookies before consent
themes.businessImpact: A first visit currently sends measurement and advertising data before the visitor has agreed to it, which can undermine trust at the point where the site first asks for attention. Visitors who notice unexpected tracking may hesitate to continue, especially when they are deciding whether to book or contact the business. The absence of a frame protection header and a content security policy header also leaves the site more exposed to unwanted embedding and script injection. That combination can weaken confidence in the site and in the business behind it.
recommendedActions: The technical team managing your site should stop measurement and advertising cookies from being written until the visitor has given consent.
Hold all third-party tracking requests until consent is recorded, because those requests already share visitor information with external providers on the first visit.
Add an X-Frame-Options header to reduce the chance of the site being embedded in a hidden frame on another site.
Add a Content-Security-Policy header with a restrictive starting policy, which will strengthen protection against injected scripts and data manipulation.

notes: No site context was provided, and the priorities therefore reflect finding severity only, not stated business goals. The findings and recommendations are based on what was measured on the affected pages, and no business type, target market, or language strategy has been inferred beyond the site evidence.
